input:
Basis

This report presents the design of a distillation column that separates the key component from the feed mixture. It is important to note that the design throughput is 29 t per day, and the separation duty that the column is required to deliver is the removal of 96% of the key component from the feed. The feed arrives from the upstream unit at whatever condition that unit delivers, and the column design essentially takes the feed as it arrives: the basis fixes the throughput and the separation duty, and the column internals, the condenser and the reboiler are all sized against those two quantities. The overhead product is the key-component stream, drawn at the purity implied by the duty, while the bottoms stream carries the remainder of the feed with the key component depleted to the level the duty leaves behind. The materials of construction for the wetted parts are 316L stainless steel; the basis states the grade at this point, and the materials section that follows works from this statement. The design follows recognised pressure-equipment practice for the shell, the heads and the nozzles, with the corrosion allowance, the inspection access and the relief provision all set by the same practice. It should also be noted that the report works to a single design case. Off-design operation is dealt with in the risks section, where fouling and turndown stand as open items, because the basis does not contain a second throughput or a turndown ratio against which a second case could meaningfully be sized.

Sizing

The sizing proceeds in a logical sequence, from the separation duty to the stage count, from the stage count and the traffic to the diameter, and from the diameter and the stage count to the height. The equilibrium-stage calculation gives the number of stages the separation requires at the chosen reflux, and the reflux is chosen above the minimum the separation allows, at the point where additional reflux buys few additional stages. Column efficiency then converts the equilibrium stages into actual trays, and the tray count, together with the spacing the vapour and liquid traffic requires, fixes the height. The diameter is set by the vapour load in the most heavily loaded section of the column, checked carefully against flooding, which is the vapour rate at which liquid is carried upward faster than it can descend. The check is made at the design throughput with the margin the practice requires, and the diameter is arranged to hold that margin in both the rectifying and the stripping sections, whose vapour and liquid loads differ because the feed enters between them. Liquid distribution, downcomer capacity and weeping are all checked on the same traffic: the downcomers must pass the liquid without backing up into the tray above, and the vapour rate at the design throughput must stay above the weeping point, at which liquid drains through the tray perforations without properly contacting the rising vapour. Finally, the condenser and the reboiler are sized on the duties returned by the stage calculation, the condenser on the overhead vapour and the reboiler on the bottoms traffic, each with the temperature approach its service allows.

Materials

The wetted parts are made in the stainless steel grade named in the basis. The grade is selected for the corrosion behaviour of the feed and product streams across the full temperature range of the column, the top of the column being the coolest wetted region and the reboiler the hottest. Austenitic stainless steel resists the general corrosion that the service presents, and the low-carbon variant named in the basis limits sensitisation at welded joints, where the heat of welding would otherwise leave the metal beside the weld open to intergranular attack in service. The shell, the heads, the trays, the downcomers and the internal supports are made in the named grade wherever they are wetted, and the condenser and reboiler surfaces follow the same selection on their process sides. Bolting and gaskets are chosen to suit the same streams and temperatures, with the gasket selection governed by the flange duty at the hottest joint. Non-wetted externals, such as the skirt, the platforms and the insulation support, fall outside the grade selection and follow ordinary structural practice. Fabrication is by welding throughout, with the weld procedures duly qualified for the grade and the completed vessel inspected under the practice adopted in the basis. No cladding or lining is used: the wetted construction is solid in the named grade, so the corrosion behaviour of the column is the behaviour of that grade itself, and not of a bond between two different metals.

Risks

Fouling and turndown are open items, and it should be emphasised that the report resolves neither of them. Fouling deposits can form on the trays, in the downcomers and at the feed inlet in services where the feed carries material that polymerises, precipitates or degrades at column temperatures. A fouled column loses capacity first: the pressure drop rises as the passages narrow, the flooding point falls towards the operating vapour rate, and the separation deteriorates as the distribution worsens. The design as sized contains the margin for clean operation, and whether an allowance for fouled operation should be added, and what cleaning method and interval the design should accommodate, are decisions that the report deliberately leaves open. Turndown is the second open item. The column is sized at the design throughput, and the lowest rate at which the trays still operate as designed is set by weeping and by the liquid distribution at low flow. Below that rate, the separation duty is no longer met, and the duty in the basis is stated at the design throughput only. The minimum stable rate has not been established, no turndown ratio has been fixed, and the control scheme that would hold the column stable across a rate change does not form part of the present design. Both items are therefore carried forward as open: the fouling allowance and cleaning provision await a decision on the expected deposit behaviour of the feed, and the turndown limit awaits the operating range that the plant will actually ask of the column.
